text: COALESCE solves a problem you've already run into: a column that's legitimately NULL sometimes, like a missing middle name, showing up raw in a report when you'd rather show a sensible fallback instead.

COALESCE checks its arguments left to right and returns the first one that isn't NULL. If MiddleName has a real value, that's what you get. If it's NULL, you get the empty string we gave it as a backup.

Here's where COALESCE goes further than a simple two-way fallback: it takes any number of arguments, checked in priority order. This query tries the phone number first, falls back to email if that's NULL, and only falls all the way back to a literal string if both are missing.

And here's a practical use beyond display: NULL propagates through arithmetic, so NULL plus anything is NULL. Wrapping a possibly-NULL operand like Freight in COALESCE stops that from silently wiping out a calculation downstream.

COALESCE only returns NULL itself in one case: when every single argument you gave it is NULL. Next up, a function that looks almost identical on the surface — ISNULL — and the genuinely tricky differences between the two.
